description:
## Goal

Give the long-lived compiler a bounded source lifecycle: withdraw and reclaim superseded code snapshots, source text, definitions, expectations, and scheduler subscriptions once no current owner refers to them.

## Current boundary

CodeMap::define always appends a new CodeId, source-map entry, text Arc, and CodeState. Same-World redefinition therefore accumulates historical source state. Exact reclamation is currently unsafe because function/module/struct expectation ownership is not yet total: late duplicate functions, named-module replacement, and stale requester expectations each have open correctness tickets.

## Strategy and proof

1. First establish durable source/definition ownership and replaceable requester contributions.
2. Define current, superseded-but-diagnostically-retained, and reclaimable states explicitly.
3. Withdraw scheduler claims, waits, product readers, span/source mappings, and semantic contributions from a superseded CodeId through normal ownership rules.
4. Reclaim only after no current diagnostic or artifact can name the snapshot.
5. Delete whole-code rediscovery scans and append-only compatibility retention made unnecessary by exact ownership.
6. Test repeated redefinition, late duplicates, macro-produced definitions, retained diagnostics, reachable/unreachable roots, and bounded inventory over many replacements.
7. Prove identical current semantics/artifacts and exact invalidation; use inventory counts rather than time thresholds.
8. Update source/module lifecycle docs and remove temporary retention probes.

Do not implement Ty or source garbage collection by age or generation heuristics.
title: Retire superseded source snapshots after exact ownership lands
